boundary_evidence: contiguous linker run: 0x020fe190..0x020fea4c, seventeen functions abutting exactly with no foreign symbol inside the span

OWNED DISPATCH TABLE (the decisive evidence): the .data table at ov002:0x0210cbb8 holds exactly fifteen function pointers, and its fifteen targets are exactly the fifteen Load*Objects functions in this span -- no sixteenth entry, and no entry pointing outside it. CORRECTED (adversarial review, was originally claimed as 'the only references'): a full sweep of config/arm9/overlays/ov002/relocs.txt finds 18 total references into/onto the span -- the 15 table loads, 2 intra-span calls to LoadObjects (both from inside Stage::LoadClsnAndObjects, so the single-caller claim below still holds), and 1 external call from arm9:0x0202d2b8 into the TU's public entry point. All three extra references support the boundary rather than contradict it.

single caller chain: _Z11LoadObjects is referenced by exactly one function in the ROM, _ZN5Stage18LoadClsnAndObjects, which is the function immediately below it in address order; nothing outside the span calls either

shared signature: fifteen of the seventeen are _Z-mangled FREE functions (no class component) whose parameter list is identical -- (LVL_Overlay::ObjSubTable&, int, unsigned) -- because LoadObjects calls them all through the one table
left boundary: _ZN3HUDC1Ev ends exactly at 0x020fe190 and is the last function of the HUD class TU (a D1/D0/C1-bearing object, plainly a different translation unit)

right boundary: the four functions at 0x020fea4c..0x020feabc are a dBgCh_Lin group, not part of this TU -- func_ov002_020fea4c and func_ov002_020fea68 copy a Vector3 out of offsets 0x0c and 0x00 of the very struct _ZN8dM3dGLin3SetERK7Vector3S2_ writes at 0x020fea84, and all four are called from one main function at 0x02037624..0x02037788. build/tu_map.json cuts at 0x020fea84 instead; this entry's cut is the corrected one.

source-order corroboration (independent of everything above): mwccarm's section order is the reverse of source order, so the original file's reading order was the reverse of the ROM's addresses. Read that way the file is exactly define-before-use -- fifteen loaders, then the dispatcher, then the public entry point -- and the loaders after LoadSimpleObjects fall in ascending handler-table index 0,1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,13,14.
boundary_caveats: NOT sinit-corroborated, and that is structural rather than an oversight: this pilot established that ZERO destructor-free TUs exist in any sinit-corroborated module of this ROM (36 corroborated modules, every one of their TUs contains a D1/D0 pair). A TU with no class cannot be constructed by a static initialiser, so the sinit gate has nothing to say about it.
ov002 as a whole is NOT sinit-corroborated (26 sinits vs 79 candidate TUs) and is not in tu_map.json's under-segmented list either.

The membership of _ZN5Stage18LoadClsnAndObjects is the one INFERENCE in this list rather than a fact. It rests on contiguity, on being LoadObjects' only caller, and on the define-before-use reading; it is externally linked, so nothing forces it into this TU the way internal linkage would. The alternative reading is a one-function TU sandwiched between HUD's object and the loader's, which is possible and is not refuted here. Dropping it leaves the other sixteen unchanged.

notes: Pilot #2 for notes/translation-unit-reconstruction-plan.md section 18. Report: notes/tu-reconstruction-pilot-2-report.md. Deliberately the opposite shape from pilot #1 (ov045/PoleLift): no class, therefore no destructor group and no vtable/RTTI, which is what this round exists to isolate.
All seventeen functions reproduce their ROM bytes when compiled together. The legacy one-function sources under src/ are untouched and remain the enrolled owners of this range.
SEVENTEEN functions, not the plan's 'approximately 5-15'. The evidence puts the boundary where it is; splitting it to hit the count would have been an invented cut.

Consolidation forced FOUR declaration conflicts that per-file compilation had been hiding, where pilot #1 found none: data_0209caa0's element type (int[] vs u8[]), data_0209f5c0's type (ActorBase* vs void*), Actor::Spawn's spelling (real static method vs hand-spelled extern "C" alias, with four mutually inconsistent copies of the alias), and func_0203accc's ARITY (decl_common.h's 1 argument vs a local 3-argument declaration -- the one no cast could reconcile). All four resolutions are byte-free; see the report.

Promotion is refused. Requires: a licensed home for the two vague-linkage Vector3 destructors, a scratch link proving the whole 0x020fe190..0x020fea4c range, and the .data phase for the dispatch table.
